title: Our Brand-New White Paper: Healthcare Innovation Depends on Data Sharing
summary: Learn how trusted data exchange enables AI, early diagnosis, and faster research. Segmed’s white paper explains the challenges and framework for secure data sharing.
body_text: Healthcare innovation is at an inflection point. Across life sciences, digital health, and clinical care, innovation is accelerating. However, it is also increasingly constrained by one fundamental issue: access to high-quality, responsibly shared data. Today, Segmed is proud to launch our latest white paper, Healthcare Innovation Depends on Data Sharing , which explores why trusted data exchange is no longer optional, and what it will take to make it work at scale. Why This White Paper, and Why Now? Healthcare has moved from paper charts and fax machines to cloud platforms, interoperable EHRs, and AI-driven analytics . Yet despite this progress, much of the world’s most valuable clinical data (particularly rich, unstructured data like medical imaging) remains locked in silos. The white paper outlines how this fragmentation slows research, delays diagnosis, and limits the potential of AI, precision medicine, and population health. It argues that fast, secure, and meaningful data sharing is now foundational to: ‍ Earlier disease detection and improved patient outcomes Faster and more representative clinical research Effective public health surveillance and response Scalable, AI-driven innovation built on real-world evidence Healthcare innovation, in other words, can only move as fast as data can move; safely, ethically, and transparently. From Reactive Care to Proactive Medicine A central theme of the paper is the shift from reactive to proactive care. When large-scale, de-identified datasets are shared responsibly, researchers can uncover early signals of disease years before symptoms appear. In areas like oncology, access to diverse, longitudinal imaging data enables AI models to detect subtle patterns that were previously invisible, unlocking the potential for earlier intervention and less invasive treatment. This shift is not theoretical. It is already reshaping how we think about diagnostics, trial design, and real-world evidence generation. The Real Barriers Aren’t Just Technical While interoperability and data quality remain challenges, the white paper goes further by examining the triad of risk that holds data sharing back: privacy, security, and regulatory uncertainty. It also highlights cultural and competitive forces (fear of misuse, misunderstanding of regulations, and the perception of data as a proprietary asset) that continue to limit collaboration. The takeaway is clear: technology alone is not enough. Sustainable data sharing requires trust , aligned incentives, and a shared commitment across stakeholders. A Framework for Trusted Data Exchange To move the industry forward, the white paper proposes a practical framework built on three interconnected pillars: ‍ Foundational governance and policy – Clear accountability, consent, and regulatory compliance that builds trust Technology and data infrastructure – Interoperability, privacy-preserving technologies, and high data quality People, culture, and collaboration – Incentives and leadership that reward openness and shared progress Together, these pillars define what responsible data sharing looks like — not as an abstract ideal, but as an operational reality. Why This Matters to Segmed At Segmed , this white paper reflects not only our perspective, but our daily commitment and foundation. Our platform exists to bridge healthcare providers and researchers by enabling secure access to diverse, multimodal real-world imaging data, while preserving patient privacy and institutional trust. From regulatory-grade datasets to AI-ready imaging infrastructure, we see firsthand how thoughtful data governance and responsible sharing accelerate discovery across the entire R&D lifecycle. This publication also features insights from our healthcare partner Fox Chase Cancer Center , illustrating how trusted collaboration can turn clinical data into a global impact. An Invitation to the Ecosystem Healthcare Innovation Depends on Data Sharing is written for healthcare leaders, researchers, technologists, policymakers, and patient advocates who are navigating the next phase of data-driven medicine. Our goal is simple: to move the conversation beyond whether data should be shared, and toward how we can do it better: securely, ethically, and at scale. We invite you to read the full white paper, explore the framework, and join us in building a healthcare ecosystem where shared data fuels better science, better care, and better outcomes for patients everywhere, without compromising trust or privacy. Read the full white paper here . ‍

title: What is a Microschool and How Do I Start One in Utah
summary: A detailed walkthrough of how you (yes, you!) can start a microschool (now!) in Utah.
body_text: Microschools are shaking up the education world in the best way possible! 🎉 These small, community-based schools prioritize personalized learning, flexible pacing, and student empowerment—giving kids an education that actually fits their needs. Unlike traditional schools, microschools offer a more dynamic, hands-on approach where kids can thrive socially and academically. Microschools are growing fast, and Prenda is at the forefront of this movement! As one of the nation’s largest and most trusted microschool networks, Prenda makes it easy and fun to start your own microschool whether you have a professional education background or not (teachers, homeschool mamas, and public school parents- you’re perfect, let’s do this!). While you can absolutely start a microschool independently, it’s a lot harder to do on your own. That’s why we built Prenda—to get all the tricky stuff out. of. your. way. So you can focus on creating a rigorous, yet whimsical , learning environment. 🤯Yes, it’s possible. This guide will walk you through Prenda’s simple 10-step process for launching a microschool in Utah—plus, we’ll cover the Utah Fits All (UFA) scholarship program that allows your students to pay your microschool feels with little to no out-of-pocket cost. Yay! So grab your favorite snack, take a deep breath, and let’s dive into how you can start your microschool adventure in Utah! It’s going to be amazing. You’re going to be amazing. 🚀 ‍ Step 1: Get Informed and Determine Your Vision You're already doing step 1! 🎉 Reading up on microschools in your area is essential. We recommend checking out these informative articles: What Are Microschools? (EdChoice) What’s a Microschool and Why Focusing on how Kids Learn is Changing Education. (Stand Together) The Rise of Millennial-Powered Microschools (Getting Smart) Consider your "why" and what type of learning environment you want to create. A significant part of this decision is your educational pedagogy and approach. At Prenda, we believe in empowering students to become self-directed learners who have strong skills and an intrinsic drive to pursue their goals. That said, there are many wonderful and beautiful ways to approach educating children. If Prenda's learning approach doesn't match your vision, that's completely okay! We want the future to be full of diverse educational options that meet everyone's unique needs. So even if you want to go it alone, we hope this process overview is a support to you in your journey! 🧳 Step 2: Set Up Your Microschool To get started, simply click " Start My Microschool " on prenda.com (or open that there link in a new tab…go on now, you got this). Starting this process in no way commits you to starting a microschool IRL. You can explore this whole idea with no commitment and no cost. You’ve got nothing to lose! After you click Start My Microschool, you'll be asked some get-to-know-you questions to help tailor the process to your needs. Follow the prompts to create and account and don’t forget to verify your email. Make sure you use the email address you want for all your Prenda communications and microschool business correspondence. Check your email and verify your account. Easy peasy! 📧 Step 3: Choose Who You Want to Serve Will you open your school to other people's children (the norm), or do you want to start with just your own kids in more of a homeschool setting with Prenda's support? This decision will shape your microschool's structure and growth potential. If you just want to homeschool with Prenda, select "Single-family Microschool," and welcome aboard! But if you want to earn an income as a microschool guide in your community, you’ll select the “Multi-family Microschool” option. Step 4: Select Your Funding Source In Utah, you have two primary funding options: direct pay or the Utah Fits All (UFA) scholarship program. The UFA program works by redirecting state education dollars to parents, allowing them to decide what type of education works best for their student. The average award amount is about $8,000 per student per year. Prenda acts as the vendor and manages all the invoicing and payment collection, so guides (that's what we call our microschool teachers!) don't have to worry about it. However (and this is kind of a big however), the UFA program is currently capped at serving about 10,000 students so it is difficult for most students to access this funding. While the law is written well and does afford some families the education choice so many are looking for, more work needs to be done before all K-12 students in Utah will have true educational freedom. If you want to support this cause in Utah, we recommend joining the Utah Education Fits All community and keeping up to date on ways you can help legislators see how important educational freedom is. Let's go Beehive State, you can do it! 🐝 For more detailed information about Utah's UFA program, check out: UFA Details Documentation Step 5: Paperwork and Safety Check At this stage you'll sign something called the "Prenda Platform Agreement." 📜 This is a simple agreement between you and Prenda that just describes the relationship between Prenda and anyone using our products and services—stuff like intellectual property use. You should know that when you use Prenda to power your microschool, you are not an employee or independent contractor. You own and operate your own independent microschool and choose to utilize Prenda's services to assist you. Signing the Prenda Platform Agreement does not commit you to running a microschool. After you sign the agreement, you'll initiate a background check for you and for any other adults that will be present during school hours. Prenda handles all the logistics and the expense of providing background checks, all you have to do is fill out your information which takes about 2 minutes. ✅ Step 6: Find a Location and Decide How Much You Will Charge As a microschool founder, you're responsible for finding your own location. The location needs to be safe for kids and have internet access. Think about creating an environment where kids can feel comfortable, be creative, and play. Many Prenda microschools operate out of homes, giving them an intimate, cozy vibe. Others use dance studios, tutoring centers, or even barns and outdoor spaces! 🏡 Here are just a few of the locations where people have run Prenda microschools... Locations Slideshow by Marketing & Media Once you have a location, it's time to decide what your income will be. Prenda guides set their own per-student rate, allowing each microschool founder to control their income. This "guide fee" is typically around $3,500-$4,000. In addition, Prenda charges a $2,199 per-student fee, bringing the total cost for families to about $$5,700-6,200 per year. 😳 While this may seem high, it's actually much less than public school per student spending, private school tuition, and other child-focused services like daycare. Plus, 99% of Prenda students use state-funded school choice scholarships, covering the cost entirely. Check out Prenda's income calculator to see how much you could earn as a microschool guide. Is Prenda worth the money? YES! We provide comprehensive training, one-on-one coaching, and access to a supportive guide community—all at no upfront cost. Our package includes K-8th curriculum for all subjects, academic coaching, and a microschool management system that makes running your school so easy. We even handle invoicing and payment collection, so you can focus on creating an exceptional learning environment. And instead of nickel and diming you with start up fees, service charges, and coaching expenses, we provide all our services with no upfront cost to you. All of our service fees are baked into that per student Prenda fee, so we only make money when you successfully launch your microschool. Pretty sweet deal, eh? We’re in your corner, no matter what. 🚩 Check out our Curriculum Overview and Guide Toolkit for a deeper dive into what you get. Step 7: Build Your Microschool Profile and Start Outreach Once you have a location and your guide fee is set, you can use Prenda's profile builder to create your microschool profile. This profile gets linked to Prenda's microschool marketplace, which is a map of all the microschools. This makes it easy for prospective parents to find you! You can also use your profile link to text to friends or post on social media. Check out the map of existing microschools here: Find a Microschool As you find interested families, all you have to do is send them an invite to join your school. They'll fill out a quick form, and bam—you'll see them pop up in your Prenda account, ready for school! Step 8: Prenda Guide Certification Training This step-by-step training will teach you more about Prenda's learning system and how kids will learn at your microschool. You'll also get sample schedules and a detailed checklist of things to help prepare you and your students for a successful year. This information will equip you to talk to parents and grow your school. 📚 At Prenda, we provide a research-aligned learning approach that allows every student to progress at their own pace without creating detrimental academic learning gaps or limiting beliefs about themselves as learners. Learning at Prenda is hands-on and focused on building real-world skills and academic mastery. 💡It's rigorous, but fun! Step 9: Your Kick-off Party Hold a school kick-off party with new students and families to get to know each other. Prenda provides details on how to run a successful school kick-off and orientation party so everyone is set up and ready for the first day. 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Creating a sense of belonging from day one sets the tone for a thriving microschool community. Step 10: Start School! What an exciting day this will be! 🎊 Microschool life is truly magical—kids get to be kids while still learning the skills they need to prepare them for the world, all without losing their love of learning. You get to watch them grow, inspire them, coach them, and cheer them on. The Prenda team will continue to support you year-round. If you have any questions or run into any issues, both our team and our guide community are here to help. You’re never alone. ‍ Want to learn more about how this all works? Drop your email to get immediate access to our free overview webinar "Microschooling 101." And if you want to hear the story of Prenda's founding and get a better sense of how the microschooling movement is revolutionizing education, check out this video... ‍ ‍

title: Healthcare Cybersecurity Strategy: Why Breach Readiness and Cyber Insurance Are Your Strongest Defense
summary: Build a stronger healthcare cybersecurity strategy by implementing breach readiness–protect patients, reduce disruption, and recover faster from cyber threats....
body_text: In healthcare, it’s understandable to hope that the right tools, safeguards, and policies will prevent a cyberattack altogether. But today’s reality is far more complex–and ultimately more empowering. The organizations with the strongest healthcare cybersecurity strategy aren’t the ones assuming they’ll never be breached. They’re the ones preparing as if a breach is inevitable. This mindset isn’t pessimistic–it’s strategic. In an era of escalating ransomware threats, adopting this strategy delivers a critical advantage and strengthens competitive differentiation. Why Healthcare Cybersecurity Requires Breach Readiness Healthcare environments face unique vulnerabilities. Interconnected electronic health records (EHRs), medical devices, third-party applications, and legacy systems create a complex digital ecosystem that is challenging to secure. Patient health information (PHI) is highly valuable, making healthcare organizations prime targets. When a breach occurs, the consequences extend beyond IT —surgeries may be delayed, medications disrupted, and regulatory reporting compromised. A modern healthcare cybersecurity strategy must anticipate breaches, not just prevent them. Preparation allows organizations to contain damage, communicate effectively, and recover quickly, protecting both patients and operational continuity. What is breach readiness in healthcare cybersecurity? The proactive preparation for cyber incidents through simulations, incident response plans, communication workflows, and cyber insurance; organizational readiness to ensure rapid response, patient safety, and operational continuity. Breach Readiness: The Heart of an Effective Healthcare Cybersecurity Strategy Preparing for a breach isn’t “planning to fail”–it’s planning to protect your patients, staff, and operations . Effective breach readiness ensures that, when a cyber incident occurs, teams act decisively. Key elements include: 1. Clear Roles and Decision Pathways Everyone–from IT to clinical staff, compliance, and communications–must know their responsibilities the moment a threat is detected. Quick coordination reduces chaos and ensures patient care continues safely. 2. Incident Response Plans Documented response plans should be regularly reviewed and tested. They outline technical containment procedures, escalation paths, and backup strategies to restore systems efficiently. 3. Tabletop Exercises Simulated cyber incidents give teams a chance to practice workflows in a controlled environment. These exercises use mock scenarios to reveal gaps, clarify communication channels, and build muscle memory for real-world events, making responses faster and more coordinated. 4. Documentation and Recordkeeping Up-to-date records of systems, backups, workflows, and security controls form the backbone of an effective response. Insurers, regulators, and internal teams rely on documentation to make informed decisions during a breach. Clear documentation also accelerates claims processing and demonstrates compliance with regulatory obligations. 5. Communication and Backup Procedures A well-defined plan specifies who notifies law enforcement, regulators, patients, staff, and insurers–and ensures that validated backups are in place to quickly restore critical systems. Combining communication clarity with tested recovery procedures protects patient safety and operational continuity. Cyber Insurance in Healthcare: A Safety Net that Strengthens Readiness A healthcare data breach can trigger overwhelming costs: technical, legal, operational, and reputational. That’s where cyber insurance in healthcare becomes critical. Modern policies do more than reimburse expenses; they typically include forensic investigation teams, legal counsel for HIPAA and state compliance, breach coaches, crisis communication support, business interruption coverage, and system restoration resources. Rapid access to these resources helps organizations respond faster, reduce confusion, and avoid costly missteps. Insurers increasingly expect maturity before they provide coverage, requiring strong authentication, endpoint protection, patching routines, and a tested incident response plan. While these requirements may feel stringent, they strengthen cyber resilience, benefiting both insurers and healthcare organizations alike. What is cyber resilience? An organization’s capacity to withstand, adapt to, and rapidly recover from cyberattacks while maintaining essential clinical and operational functions. It goes beyond prevention, emphasizing continuity, restoration, and long-term strength. Building Cyber Resilience in Healthcare Through Preparedness Healthcare organizations with strong cyber resilience share several key traits, including: Regular simulations: Conducting exercises quarterly or biannually, rather than once-a-year check-the-box events. Clinical leader engagement: Actively involving clinical leaders to ensure patient safety is fully integrated into the cybersecurity action plan. Rehearsed communication workflows: Practicing coordinated messaging for staff, patients, regulators, and the broader community. A continuous improvement mindset: Treating breach preparation as an ongoing process , refining procedures and strengthening systems after each exercise. While cyberattacks cannot be eliminated, robust governance prevents the disruption that usually follows. Benefits of a Mature Cybersecurity Action Plan A well-practiced healthcare cybersecurity action plan offers benefits that extend beyond IT, including: Faster system restoration: Reducing downtime and minimizing associated financial losses. Lower financial risk: Decreasing the likelihood of paying ransom during an attack. Improved regulatory readiness: Strengthening preparedness for audits, reporting, and compliance requirements. Greater patient and community trust: Demonstrating transparency, confidence, and control during disruption. Stronger cyber insurance outcomes: Aligning with insurer expectations to improve claim speed, success, and long-term insurability. In healthcare, trust and safety are everything. A confident, coordinated response during a cyber incident protects both. Preparedness Over Fear: A New Cybersecurity Mindset A breach is no longer a sign of failure–it’s a sign of the times. What truly matters is how ready your organization is to respond. Embracing an “assume-breach mindset” signals maturity, not defeat. For healthcare leaders, the path to resilience is clear: cybersecurity in healthcare is about preparation, not panic. By embracing breach readiness, your organization can reduce disruption, protect patients, and build trust. Ready to strengthen your breach response strategy? Contact our expert team today to learn how Health Catalyst can help you build a resilient cybersecurity action plan. ‍

title: Malama Health Awarded $2.4M Fast Track SBIR Grant from NIH to Prevent Type 2 Diabetes in Postpartum Women
body_text: SAN FRANCISCO — Malama Health , a privately held San Francisco-based health technology company focused on improving maternal health outcomes, announced that the National Institutes of Health (NIH) has awarded the Phase I portion ($314K) of its Fast Track Phase I/II ($2.4M total) Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) grant. The grant aims to reduce the progression to type 2 diabetes (T2D) in women who experienced gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) during pregnancy. The project will develop a novel risk-stratification algorithm that integrates biological, clinical, and social health data to identify which women are at greatest risk of developing T2D - a condition that affects up to 70% of women with prior GDM within 20 years. Malama will then implement an AI-driven, personalized postpartum diabetes prevention program aligned to individual risk levels, integrating digital coaching, wraparound care management, and a tech-enabled delivery of the CDC’s PreventT2 curriculum adapted specifically for postpartum. In the Phase I portion of the grant, to be completed in Q1 2026, Malama Health will expand its existing dataset of over 40,000 users to ensure stronger representation across groups at high-risk for gestational diabetes. The team will then develop and validate a risk algorithm to stratify postpartum individuals based on their clinical, biometric, and social risk factors for T2D. Orlando Li, Malama Health’s Chief Technology Officer and Co-Investigator on the study, noted that “Malama’s algorithms combine structured data like glucose levels, weight, and blood pressure values with unstructured inputs such as meal images and structural risk data, allowing us to create precise, personalized interventions that can improve outcomes over the long term.” In Phase II , to be completed by mid-2028, Malama will launch and refine a tailored digital diabetes prevention program that delivers personalized care plans to users based on their risk level. The program will integrate with clinical workflows at Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) and be supported by health coaches, community health workers, and maternal-fetal medicine specialists. Outcomes will include engagement, improved glucose trends, and reduced incidence of T2D within the first postpartum year. Malama Health’s Chief Executive Officer and Principal Investigator on the grant, Mika Eddy, who previously had gestational diabetes underscored that “the pregnancy period is a golden window of opportunity to improve health not only for mom, but for baby - and baby’s babies - offering a unique opportunity to fundamentally shift and improve health over generations. While diabetes prevention programs are not new, this will be the first tailored to the postpartum period, integrating the lived experience of birth and the barriers many women, especially those insured by Medicaid, face when accessing care. We’re excited to build on the insights from tens of thousands of users who have used Malama’s app during pregnancy and to deliver care to dramatically improve health outcomes.” Visit http://www.heymalama.com to learn more about Malama’s platform and Medicaid-focused services for maternal wellness and chronic disease prevention.

title: How Alex Mahl increased sales on Poshmark by 500% with Photoroom
summary: Discover how Alexandra Mahl uses Photoroom to create consistent product image backgrounds and drive sales for her consignment reselling business.
body_text: Life before Photoroom Tried multiple backgrounds (rugs, doors, sheets) but nothing looked clean Listings hardly showed up in Google search results Struggled to stand out while selling saturated products Used manual process for creating product and promotional visuals Life with Photoroom Sales increased by 500% Listings appear at top of Google search within 15 minutes Batch-edits 10 listings in 3 minutes/20-30 listings in a day using Batch Manages visuals for nearly 8,000 active listings while working full-time Professional photos build buyer trust and confidence Alex Mahl didn't set out to become a reseller when she started selling her own clothes 10 years ago. At 18, she was simply helping her parents move and needed to clear out her closet. But what began as a closet clean-out quickly evolved into a side business. "I started helping other people local to me sell their own clothing as well," Alex recalls. During the COVID-19 pandemic period, she’d go to clients' homes and help them list their items on Poshmark for an hourly fee. But Alex, who works full-time as an office manager and at a law firm’s finance department, knew she needed a more sustainable business model. "It was getting very overwhelming, and I wasn't really able to focus on my own closet anymore,” shares Alex. “I was like, okay, I'm helping all these people make all this money. Yes, I'm making an hourly fee, but what can I do to make it better for myself as well?" From personal decluttering to a consignment business At first, Alex stopped her one-to-one listing offer. She then hired people across New York to thrift clothing items for her business, managed the listing process on her shop, and hosted livestream sales shows on Poshmark to build her brand presence. But the real turning point came after her New York Times feature story caught the attention of a celebrity with 1.2 million followers, who contacted Alex to sell her items on consignment. Two weeks later, Alex picked up 14 garbage bags of designer clothing, and her business model changed fully to consignment. As a consignee, she now receives items from individuals and only pays them after the item sells. This advantage wasn’t possible in the previous model, which required her to pay thrifters upfront even if shoppers didn’t end up buying the item. “Working with thrifters wasn't terrible, but I wasn't seeing as much profit as I wanted to because I was constantly paying off my credit card.” — Alexandra Mahl, Founder, APM FINDS, LLC. Today, Alex runs a successful Poshmark shop , where she has nearly 8,000 active listings. She’s been featured in Business Insider , appeared in a Poshmark TV commercial, and even spoke on a Photoroom panel at PoshFest . With this growth and a steady stream of consignment clients, she began exploring ways to improve her products’ presentation online. But she faced a product image problem that limited her strategy. The photography problem that was limiting growth As a Poshmark ambassador and savvy e‑commerce entrepreneur, Alex knew that product visuals with clean backgrounds help boost online sales. And yet she couldn't find the perfect backdrops. “Think of Poshmark store profiles like dating apps. If your first photo isn’t aesthetically pleasing, no one's going to click on it. So, I tried different scenes in my house to capture products in the best backdrops. But no matter what I did, whether it was a rug, the back of my door, all my sheets, the image background just didn't look clean.” — Alexandra Mahl, Founder, APM FINDS, LLC. Nothing gave her the professional, polished look she needed. And Alex needed every advantage she could get in the competitive resale market, especially when reselling items from popular brands like Lululemon. "I thought, well, Lululemon is a saturated market. How am I going to make my item sell over someone else's?" shares Alex. Between her full-time job and listing 20-30 items per day, plus packing 10-20 packages every night, Alex needed a solution that could transform her basic iPhone photos into professional-looking product images without adding hours to her already packed workload . And so she went searching. Alex found her visual partner in Photoroom She explored Google for a solution, looking for a platform that could remove backgrounds and replace them with cleaner ones, like white backgrounds or marble flooring. That's how she discovered Photoroom. “I’m serious about my business. So, once I found Photoroom, I knew it was the right solution for me and paid for it instantly. I didn't even do a free trial because I was already sold.” — Alexandra Mahl, Founder, APM FINDS, LLC. Today, Alex uses Photoroom to edit images for 20-30 items daily. Her workflow takes just three minutes for 10 listings: She starts by snapping 10 products and listing them on Poshmark. Next, she opens the Photoroom app , selects the Batch feature , uploads all first images of the items she listed, waits a few seconds for the tool to automatically remove the image backgrounds and add white backgrounds , and saves the edited photos in her camera roll. Finally, she returns to her Poshmark app and changes the first picture of each listing, replacing the old images with the newly edited ones. She now has multiple solutions for standing out on Poshmark Her strategy combines Photoroom's professional imagery with smart marketing through social media , live shows, and audience engagement to stand out from the competition. But the foundation is always the same: a clean first photo that compels people to click. While Alex primarily edits backgrounds with Photoroom, she also uses the platform to: Showcase clothing on virtual models She uses the AI virtual models for apparel , allowing her to show how items look when worn, without needing to style them on a person. "I love how I can just post a black t-shirt and press the button and boom, it's on a model," she says. "And if I don't like the model that it's on, I could change it." Resize images to fit any e‑commerce platform She also relies on Photoroom's platform-specific optimization, most notably through the image resizer . "I like how you're able to pick the image layout for each resale platform in Photoroom. If you click the feature, it will show sizes for Poshmark, eBay, Mercari, and Depop. Photoroom already knows the exact square footage that your image needs for the platform. That's a big deal in e‑commerce." — Alexandra Mahl, Founder, APM FINDS, LLC. Create marketing materials Alex has found creative ways to extend Photoroom's value beyond her daily listings. When she was hosting live selling shows three times a week, she used Photoroom to create eye-catching promotional flyers . "I would grab things out of pictures, remove all the white backgrounds, and then create my flyer," she shares. "Those were huge for me because it drew everyone to my shows." Today, cleaner photos help her shop appear on Google Search, boosting sales by 500% "My biggest win is that my listings show up on Google, and it's because I now have that white crisp background from Photoroom.” — Alexandra Mahl, Founder, APM FINDS, LLC. This matters because Poshmark's internal search function is notoriously unreliable. "The search on Poshmark is not great if you're looking for something specific," Alex explains. "Nine times out of ten, what you’re searching for won’t come up. So Google is a better channel for searching." By optimizing her product photos for Google's algorithms, Alex essentially created a second storefront, one that captures buyers who would never have found her through Poshmark's platform alone and has skyrocketed her sales as a result. “I've actually tested this out with my own listings. I'll give it like 15 minutes after I list it, then I'll Google it, and my product will show up right at the top. That's a big deal. Just adding white backgrounds using Photoroom has made my sales jump by 500%.” — Alexandra Mahl, Founder, APM FINDS, LLC. Beyond visibility and sales, Alex continues to rely on Photoroom as her product visual partner that helps her: Build buyers’ trust: For Alex, professional photos do more than drive clicks; they build buyer confidence in an industry where trust is everything. "The resale market can be scary. I've ordered things that didn’t look as described,” she says. “So I'm always making sure my items are accurately displayed and described." Save time for what matters most: Alex has scaled her business without sacrificing her sanity or full-time job. She's able to manage nearly 8,000 active listings, work with high-profile consignment clients, and maintain a sustainable business model that's funding major life milestones, including buying her first car and planning her wedding. Alex is looking ahead with confidence Alex continues to expand her consignment client roster while maintaining her full-time career, confident that Photoroom will scale with her ambitions. title: The Dilution Effect: When Everyone Has the Credential, No One Does
summary: The market knowledge your talent decisions depend on — centralized. Verata unifies company intelligence, executive data, and search management in one platform built for PE talent and executive search.
body_text: The dilution effect creates a specific, exploitable market inefficiency. If your competitors are paying a premium -- in search fees, in time, in opportunity cost -- to secure candidates with credentials that do not predict outcomes, then you can achieve equivalent expected outcomes at lower cost by widening your aperture. The firms that recognize this dynamic first will benefit in three ways. Deeper talent pool. Dropping the prior-CEO-experience requirement immediately expands your candidate universe by roughly 50%. These are candidates who are being systematically overlooked by an industry that has convinced itself this credential matters. The data says it does not. Lower acquisition cost. Candidates without the 'perfect' resume are in lower demand. They command lower compensation premiums, require less search effort to identify, and are more likely to accept. You are not sacrificing expected performance by hiring them. You are paying less for equivalent expected outcomes. Faster deployment. The search for a candidate who checks every credential box is slow. A search that relaxes non-predictive criteria is faster. In PE, where every month of CEO vacancy is a month of value creation delay, speed has direct financial value. When everyone has the credential, it stops being a signal. It becomes a minimum threshold. The industry increased its selection pressure on prior CEO experience by 50% over eighteen years. The predictive return was zero. The firms that act on this finding will widen their aperture, access a deeper talent pool at lower cost, and deploy leadership faster -- while their competitors continue to compete for a narrowing pool of 'credentialed' candidates whose credentials do not predict the outcome that matters.

title: Does WellSky Have a CRM? What Home Care Agencies Should Know
summary: WellSky is built for operations, not relationships. Here is what that gap means for your agency.
body_text: WellSky is one of the most widely used agency management systems in home care. It handles scheduling, billing, EVV, and care coordination well. But if you have ever tried to track a referral source, follow up with a prospective client, or manage your intake pipeline inside WellSky, you have probably noticed something: it was not built for that. So does WellSky have a CRM? The short answer is no, not in any meaningful sense. WellSky is an operational platform, not a relationship management tool. And for home care agencies trying to grow, that distinction matters a lot. Understanding what non-medical home care software actually needs to include before committing to a tech stack can save you from expensive gaps like this one. What WellSky Actually Does WellSky is an agency management system (AMS). It is designed to run the operational side of your home care business once a client is active. The platform covers caregiver scheduling, payroll integration, visit verification, billing, and clinical documentation. For mid-sized to larger agencies with established client rosters, WellSky handles a heavy operational load. What it does not do is manage the front end of your business: the leads, the referral partners, the intake calls, the follow-up emails, and the pipeline from first contact to signed client. These are CRM functions, and WellSky was not built to handle them. What a CRM Does That WellSky Cannot A home care CRM manages relationships before and during the sales process. That means tracking every lead, logging every call with a referral partner, sending follow-up emails, and giving you a clear view of where each prospective client stands in your intake pipeline. Here is a direct comparison of what each tool covers: Function WellSky Home Care CRM Active client scheduling Yes No Billing and payroll Yes No EVV and visit verification Yes No Referral source tracking No Yes Lead and inquiry management No Yes Follow-up email automation No Yes Intake pipeline visibility No Yes Call logging and activity history No Yes Care plan drafting from intake No Yes The gap is significant. If you are relying on WellSky alone to manage incoming leads and referral relationships, you are likely using spreadsheets, sticky notes, or memory to fill in what WellSky cannot do. According to data from a survey of 500-plus home care consumers , response time and follow-through are the top factors families consider when choosing an agency. Without a CRM layer, those follow-ups fall through the cracks. Why Referral Management Is the Real Issue For most home care agencies, the majority of new clients come from referral sources: hospital discharge planners, social workers, senior living communities, and physicians. These are relationship-based channels. The agency that stays in front of referral partners, responds quickly, and documents every interaction wins more business. WellSky does not track referral source activity. There is no place to log your last call with a hospital discharge coordinator, no way to see which referral sources sent you the most clients this quarter, and no pipeline view showing how many inquiries are sitting at each stage of intake. For a small agency competing against larger players with dedicated marketing staff, this is a real disadvantage. If you are also evaluating how WellSky compares to other AMS platforms like AxisCare, the referral and CRM limitations are worth factoring into that decision. You can dig into the broader software landscape in this 2026 guide to the best non-medical home care software . The Two-System Problem Most Agencies Face Because WellSky does not include CRM functionality, agencies end up building a patchwork of tools to cover the gap. Some common combinations: WellSky for operations plus a spreadsheet for leads and referrals WellSky plus a generic CRM like HubSpot or Salesforce not built for home care WellSky plus nothing, relying on staff memory and email inboxes None of these work well. Generic CRMs require heavy customization to fit home care workflows and still do not connect back to your AMS data. Spreadsheets do not scale, and they are invisible to anyone who is not maintaining them. Many agencies eventually reach the point where moving from spreadsheets into a more structured system for home care operations becomes unavoidable. The question is which CRM layer actually fits home care and connects cleanly to your existing AMS. How Sage Care Fills the Gap Sage Care is a HIPAA-compliant client intake automation platform built specifically for home care agencies. It adds the CRM and intake layer that WellSky does not provide, and it integrates directly with WellSky and AxisCare so your data stays in sync. Here is what Sage Care handles that WellSky cannot: Lead and inquiry management Every inbound inquiry is logged automatically. You can see every prospective client, where they are in the pipeline, and what the next step is, without digging through emails or notes. Intake automation after calls and assessments After every intake call or in-home assessment, Sage Care's AI generates a call summary, a draft follow-up email, care plan updates, and record suggestions. Your staff reviews, edits if needed, and approves in one tap. What used to take 15 to 30 minutes now takes under 5. Referral source tracking Sage Care tracks every referral partner, logs all communication, and gives you a clear activity history so you know which relationships are active and which need attention. Bidirectional AMS sync Sage Care syncs patient data and care plans with WellSky and AxisCare. When a lead converts to a client, the record moves into your AMS without duplicate data entry. You can see how this works in detail on the Sage Care and WellSky integration page . Built-in VOIP Sage Care includes inbound and outbound calling on iOS, call recording, and automatic logging to patient and contact records. Every call with a referral partner or prospective client is captured and tied to the right record. The result is a complete picture of your agency's pipeline from first inquiry through active client, all connected to your WellSky or AxisCare data. For agencies working to understand how a CRM layer fits into their overall software stack, this complete 2026 guide to AI intake software for home care walks through the full picture. Who This Matters Most For The WellSky-plus-CRM gap is most painful for small and growing agencies. If you have a lean team and every lead matters, losing a prospective client because a follow-up slipped through the cracks is not a minor inconvenience. It is lost revenue. Larger agencies with dedicated intake coordinators and marketing staff can absorb some of this inefficiency because they have people to manually track and follow up. Owner-operators and small teams cannot. For them, a structured home care CRM is not a nice-to-have. It is what makes the difference between consistent lead conversion and chasing leads reactively. Ready to Close the Gap? If your agency runs on WellSky or AxisCare and you are managing intake and referrals with spreadsheets or improvised tools, Sage Care is built for exactly this situation. It adds the CRM and intake automation layer your AMS cannot provide, and connects back to your existing system without double data entry. Schedule a demo to see how Sage Care works alongside WellSky and AxisCare. Sage Care also offers a 30-day free trial so you can see the impact on your intake workflow before you commit. Frequently Asked Questions Does WellSky include lead tracking or referral management? No. WellSky is an agency management system focused on operations for active clients. It does not include lead tracking, referral source management, or intake pipeline tools. Can I use WellSky and a CRM together? Yes. Many agencies use WellSky for operations and a separate CRM for intake and referral management. Sage Care integrates directly with WellSky so data stays in sync between both systems. What is the difference between an AMS and a CRM in home care? An AMS manages active clients: scheduling, billing, EVV, and care plans. A CRM manages prospective clients and referral relationships before and during the intake process. Most agencies need both.

title: 2026 Subaru WRX Pricing, Specs, and Release Date
summary: While it may look identical to last year's model, the 2026 Subaru WRX adds appeal with the addition of a value base trim.
body_text: The Subaru WRX is a sporty compact sedan with standard all-wheel drive (AWD) and grin-inducing handling. Competitors include the Volkswagen GTI, the Honda Civic Type R, and the Toyota GR Corolla. 2026 Subaru WRX Pricing, Specs, and Release Date What’s New for the 2026 Subaru WRX Design Powertrain Interior Technology Safety Pricing and Release Date Further Research What’s New for the 2026 Subaru WRX The WRX’s prices climbed sky-high for the 2025 model year, but they’re now back at a more reasonable level. In addition to a price cut across the lineup, the base WRX reappears, slotting underneath the Premium trim with minimal equipment but an even lower price of entry. Proximity key entry and push-button start now come standard. Those with a higher budget should check out the limited-edition Series.Yellow, based on the performance tS trim. Design The WRX has had the same basic yet distinctive shape for years, with an unobtrusive hood scoop up front and a subtle flip on the decklid out back, with big wheels framed by matte fender flares and lower body trim. There isn’t much reason to change it, as a well-designed sedan always looks good and it gives the WRX a ton of practical appeal. For those looking for something a little different from the typical WRX in ubiquitous World Rally Blue paint, the Series.Yellow is an eye-catcher, with Sunrise Yellow paint and matte black-painted alloy wheels. Powertrain Subaru equips the WRX with the same powertrain across the lineup, though the top trim levels have some subtle tuning differences for more distinctive performance. The WRX features a turbocharged flat-four engine rated at 271 horsepower and 258 pound-feet of torque, standard AWD, and a choice of a six-speed manual or a continuously variable transmission (CVT). Though the CVT gets paddle shifters to enhance the fun factor, the WRX’s six-speeder is one of the most entertaining manuals still on the market. The GT and tS feature adaptive dampers for an even more pinned-down suspension feel and better handling. The GT comes only with the performance CVT, while the tS comes only with the manual transmission, and also gets Brembo brakes. Manual versions are rated for 22 mpg combined, and the CVT versions get 21 mpg combined. Interior The Subaru WRX seats five, with plenty of room in the front row and a snug second row. In all versions, the design is on the basic side, but higher trims are dressed up with power-adjustable and heated front seats, available snugly bolstered Recaro bucket seats, synthetic suede upholstery, and sporty two-tone color combinations. Touches such as ambient lighting and alloy pedals complete the racing-inspired effect. The WRX’s trunk is on the small side, at just 12.4 cubic feet. Technology The WRX features the same 11.6-inch, portrait-oriented touchscreen standard across the Subaru lineup. Though wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, the system itself isn’t the best. The menus are crowded, burying functions that should be operated by physical controls, such as the heated seats and the driving modes. Inputs are sluggish, too. Available upgrades are scarce, but the premium Harman Kardon stereo is nice.
